newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sept forex reserves up to $86.4 bln - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sept forex reserves up to $86.4 bln - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign-exchange reserves edged up to about US$86.4 billion at the end of September from $86.387 billion a month earlier, the Economic Daily News said on Tuesday.
The paper called the figure an estimate and attributed the small rise chiefly to foreign-exchange rate changes.
The central bank refused to comment, saying it would release the official figure on October 24.
Taiwan's forex reserves, the world's third-largest after Japan and China, fell in late 1995 and early 1996 as political tensions with rival China intensified into a military crisis in March.

Beijing, determined to thwart any moves toward Taiwan's independence, held months of war games and missile tests in the Taiwan strait in the run-up to Taiwan's March 23 presidential polls, triggering waves of U.S. dollar-buying and a run on gold.

The central bank intervened during the crisis to support the Taiwan dollar and the island's hypersensitive stock market. The trend reversed after the election and the start of a clear easing of tensions with China, with foreign reserves rising slowly since April.
Foreign reserves peaked at $100.412 billion in June 1995 -- the same month that Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui made a private but high-profile U.S. visit, sparking the standoff with China.

Since a civil war split them in 1949, Beijing has regarded Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a renegade province ineligible for sovereign international ties and opposes any shift from Taiwan's official policy of eventual reunification with the mainland.
